task.title: storypole list --status X ignores the archived filter, so an archived backlog still lists as verified

acceptance_criteria:
REPRODUCED 2026-11-06.

  storypole list                      -> 64 rows   (archived excluded)
  storypole list --include-archived   -> 293 rows  (everything)
  storypole list --status verified    -> 221 rows  (all of them archived)

All 221 verified tasks were archived in this session (227 tasks carry a task_archived event and none carry task_unarchived), yet --status verified still lists all 221. Supplying --status therefore drops the archived filter that the unfiltered view applies, so the two views disagree about what 'verified' contains.

How it surfaced: I ran the archive sweep and the verified count did not move, so I concluded the sweep had failed and started checking the ledger by hand. It had worked. A filter that silently widens its own scope when you add a narrow term is worse than a filter that errors, because it produces confident wrong answers about the state of the backlog - and this session has spent a lot of effort on exactly that failure mode.

Expected: status and archive are orthogonal (SP-27), so --status verified should compose with the default archived-excluded view and report 0. --include-archived should be the only way to widen it.
